newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia's Alfa-Group seeks control of TNK.
newsitem.headline: Russia's Alfa-Group seeks control of TNK.

text.p: Russia's Alfa-Group, which won 40 percent of Tyumen Oil Company TNK last Friday, is seeking a majority stake through a forthcoming auction for a further 48.68 percent of the company, an Alfa-Group official said on Thursday.

"We will definitely take part in the next tender," said German Khan, President of oil trading company Alfa-Eko, which is part of the Alfa-Group. "We will try to go up to a controlling stake," he told reporters.

The 40 percent stake in Tyumenskaya Neftyanaya Kompaniya (TNK) was won last Friday at an investment tender by Novy Kholding, a unit of Alfa-Group's Alfa-Bank. The winning bid was $810 million, including the price of the shares and other investment conditions.
The government is offering 48.68 percent of TNK in a further auction from August 5 to September 24. It is a cash auction, and does not have to be bought in one block.

Khan said Novy Kholding (New Holding) would pay off all debts belonging to TNK subsidiaries by the end of the year. It would invest the remainder of the sum, around $600 million, in projects including rebuilding the troubled Ryazan refinery and renovating the huge but uneconomic Samotlor oil field, part of TNK's main output unit, Nizhnevartovskneftegaz.
TNK produced 21.3 million tonnes of crude oil in 1996 (426,000 barrels per day), down slightly from 22.6 million (452,000 bpd) in 1995, making it the sixth largest oil producer in Russia.
